scope: All 3 exact systems Teach bodies independently reviewed against each canonical objective, constraints, key and topic prerequisites, and all curriculum exemplars. Every proposed worked result was independently recomputed. The four changed positive-coefficient inequality solution sketches were independently reread; their operation sequence now matches the unchanged answers and lesson concepts. No proposal or live-content approval.

records.canonical_objective: Set up two equations from a sum/difference
records.canonical_constraints: define two variables; one relationship per sentence

curriculum_exemplars_reviewed.problem: Two numbers have sum $17$ and difference $5$. Define larger $x$, smaller $y$; find $(x,y)$.
Two classes have $48$ students combined. Class X has $6$ more than class Y. Define their sizes $x,y$ and find $(x,y)$.
A table records total mass $25$ kg and heavier-minus-lighter mass $3$ kg. Define masses $x,y$ and find (heavier, lighter).
A learner swaps sum and difference for two lengths totaling $30$ cm with difference $8$ cm. Define longer $x$, shorter $y$ and find $(x,y)$.

records.worked_problem: The sum of two numbers is $34$ and their difference is $12$. Find the numbers.
records.semantic_reasoning: Defines larger and smaller explicitly, translates sum and difference in the correct order, solves, and reports requested units/order.
records.independent_arithmetic_evidence: x+y=34 and x-y=12 add to 2x=46, so x=23,y=11; sum 34 and difference 12.

curriculum_exemplars_reviewed.problem: A rectangle has perimeter $34$ cm and length $3$ cm more than width. Find (length, width) in cm.
Two supplementary angles differ by $40$ degrees. Find (larger, smaller) in degrees.
Two ages sum to $38$ years; one person is $12$ years older. Find (older, younger).
A learner treats complementary angles as totaling $180$. They differ by $10$ degrees. Find the correct (larger, smaller) angles.

records.worked_problem: A father is $4$ times as old as his son, and the sum of their ages is $55$. Find each age.
records.semantic_reasoning: Covers rectangle perimeter, complementary/supplementary totals, and age sum/difference/ratio setups without using later skills.
records.independent_arithmetic_evidence: f=4s and f+s=55 give 5s=55, so son=11 and father=44.

records.canonical_constraints: one scaled relationship plus one sum; integer answers

curriculum_exemplars_reviewed.problem: Two numbers sum to $23$; the first is twice the second plus $2$. Find (first, second).
A group has $35$ adults and children combined; there are $3$ more than three times as many children as adults. Find (adults, children).
Two tanks total $50$ L; tank A holds $5$ L less than four times tank B. Find (A, B) volumes.
A learner multiplies the whole total by $2$ when one length is $2$ cm more than twice another and their sum is $20$ cm. Find (longer, shorter).

records.worked_problem: Two numbers sum to $48$; three times the larger minus the smaller is $64$. Find the numbers.
records.semantic_reasoning: Keeps the scaled relationship separate from the sum, preserves which quantity is multiplied, and verifies both relations.

limitations: Semantic review only. Receipts are rebound to the post-repairs curriculum snapshot after exact diff review. Production gates were outside this review; no proposal files or live content were modified.
